page.layout: One page of text. Running head at top centre, page number at top right. Below the running head, a centred italic heading of two lines. One column of running text, with a drop-cap initial. Catchword at bottom right, gathering signature at bottom left. Right margin shows only show-through and bleed from the other side, so no marginal notes are transcribed.

main_text.head: Status & fortuna civitatis Attica post mortem Alexandri M.
main_text.p: Porrò civitatis Atticæ status popularis post xxx tyrannos eversos incolumis stetit usque ad mortem Alexandri Magni, per annos quasi lxxx. Eo Babylone defuncto cum Antipater Macedoniæ præfectus exules Athenas & in alias urbes Græciæ reducere pararet, id quod Alexander ipse, si vixisset, facere constituerat, bellum contra eum ab Atheniensibus & sociis motum: quo primum victus in Theslàlia, deinde auxiliis à Cratero acceptis victor, cæso cum ex-ercitu Leosthene duce Attico ad Lamiam urbem, belli vim in Athenienses recenti clade perculsos convertit, ipsas Athenas obsedit, & in eas angustias re-degit, ut se certis legibus dedere coge-rentur. Leges dictæ, ut dimisso statu popularis pauciorum imperio civitas rege-retur, quorum census non minor esset bis mille drachmis, & præsidium Macedonum ad avertendos vulgi motus in arce Munychia, quæ inter Piræum & Phalerum media est cum portu ad mare sita, urbique Atticæ proxima, recipe-retur. Ita urbis imperium summum ab universa civium multitudine ad ditio-res numero novies mille, qui tantum in censu

page.notes: Right margin: faint red-tinted fragments and mirrored text are show-through from the reverse side, and were left out. Left and bottom-right edges show the neighbouring page and digitiser marks, also left out. The signature "M 5" is uncertain: the figure may be a long s, so it is marked [?]. The heading's italic is transcribed as a level 2 title. "Theslàlia" keeps the printed accent on the à.
